title: A molecular electron density theory investigation the regio- and stereoselectivity of the 32CA reaction between 1-pyrroline nitrone and dihydrofuran
content: In the present study, the mechanistic and selectivity features governing the nitrone-mediated (3 + 2) cycloaddition between 3,4-dihydro-2H-pyrrole 1-oxide (nitrone 1) and 2,3-dihydrofuran 2 were comprehensively investigated within the framework of Molecular Electron Density Theory (MEDT) at the M06-2X-D3/6-311G(d,p) computational level. Electron Localization Function (ELF) analysis classified nitrone 1 as a zwitterionic three-atom component (zw-TAC), while the Conceptual Density Functional Theory (CDFT) descriptors indicated a low-polarity cycloaddition with a weak electron-density transfer from dihydrofuran 2 toward nitrone 1. Exploration of the potential energy surface revealed a highly regio- and stereoselective one-step mechanism that preferentially leads to the exo cycloadduct, in excellent agreement with experimental observations. The calculated global electron density transfer (GEDT) at the most favorable transition state, TS1-x, was only 0.033e, demonstrating the very small magnitude of electron-density transfer and supporting the null electron-density flux (NEDF) character of the reaction. Bonding Evolution Theory (BET) analysis showed that bond formation occurs after the transition state through a progressive reorganization of the electron density accompanied by the generation of pseudoradical centers. Moreover, Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM), Non-Covalent Interaction (NCI), and Independent Gradient Model (IGM) analyses demonstrated that attractive noncovalent interactions play a crucial role in stabilizing the favored transition state and governing the observed regio- and stereoselectivity.
